interest: Shows 1940 caution over Japan's imperial-anniversary essay contest, and 1944 planning to exploit Japanese diplomatic archives after surrender.
overview: This file (decimal file 894.414, 'History., Japan, Public Records.') covers State Department records between March 1940 and September 1944 relating to Japanese public records, cultural relations, and enemy archives. The earlier segment (March 1940) concerns an invitation from Matsuzo Nagai of the Kokusai Bunka Shinkokai (Society for International Cultural Relations) to promote a worldwide essay contest commemorating the 2,600th anniversary of the founding of the Japanese Empire. The Division of Cultural Relations and Division of Far Eastern Affairs coordinated a restrained response, noting that scholarship prize funds would need to be spent within Japan and advising that no action be taken beyond notifying the U.S. Consulate General in Tokyo. The later document (September 1944) addresses post-war planning by the Interdivisional Area Committee regarding the recruitment and training of personnel needed to seize, examine, and analyze the anticipated vast volume of Japanese diplomatic and consular files upon Japan's unconditional surrender, noting that preparations were lagging due to the prioritization of European operations.

subfiles.about: Memorandum concerning the need for adequate trained personnel to seize and examine Japanese diplomatic and consular files upon the unconditional surrender of Japan.
subfiles.summary: Kahn warns that examining Japan's enemy files after defeat will exceed current staff, as Far East planning lags behind Europe.
subfiles.title: Office Memorandum from Walter Kahn to Abbot L. Moffat on Staffing to Examine Enemy Files

subfiles.about: Internal memorandum from the Division of Far Eastern Affairs offering no objection to acknowledging Matsuzo Nagai's letter regarding an essay contest.
subfiles.from: Division of Far Eastern Affairs (Joseph W. Ballantine)
subfiles.summary: Memo on acknowledging Nagai's essay-contest letter, noting its scholarship funds must be spent entirely within Japan.
subfiles.title: Memorandum from Division of Far Eastern Affairs regarding Acknowledgment of Matsuzo Nagai's Letter

subfiles.about: Memorandum requesting the views of the Division of Far Eastern Affairs on participating in the 26th Centennial International Essay Contest of Japan.
subfiles.summary: Thomson asks Far Eastern Affairs whether to cooperate modestly with Japan's 2,600th-anniversary essay contest.
subfiles.title: Memorandum from Charles A. Thomson to Division of Far Eastern Affairs regarding Essay Contest Inquiry

subfiles.about: Letter from the Kokusai Bunka Shinkokai inviting U.S. participation and publicity for an international essay contest commemorating the 2,600th anniversary of the Japanese Empire.
subfiles.summary: Nagai announces a worldwide essay contest for Japan's 2,600th imperial anniversary, asking Cherrington to circulate it.
subfiles.title: Letter from Matsuzo Nagai to Ben Cherrington Announcing the 26th Centennial International Essay Contest

subfiles.about: Memorandum advising that no action be taken on the Kokusai Bunka Shinkokai letter beyond sending an instruction to the U.S. Consulate General in Tokyo.
subfiles.from: Division of Far Eastern Affairs (Maxwell M. Hamilton / Cabot Coville)
subfiles.summary: Far Eastern Affairs recommends only forwarding an instruction to Tokyo, taking no further action on Japan's essay contest.
subfiles.title: Memorandum from Division of Far Eastern Affairs to Division of Cultural Relations regarding Action on Essay Contest Letter
